summary: Historic fire lookout tower on Mount Hallowell in Spipiyus Provincial Park; BC Parks says it was recently restored.

access.note: In Spipiyus Provincial Park; the summit is reached on foot by a well-maintained 1.5 km trail. BC Parks describes the old lookout as a fine place to take in the view.

visit.trail_note: 1.5 km (0.93 mi) well-maintained trail from the park to the summit tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: SummitPost describes the tower as unused for an unknown time and BC Parks says it was recently restored. Neither page is dated, so the BC Parks statement is used for the present condition.

sources.title: Fire Lookouts of British Columbia: History, Hikes & Where to Stay

notes_for_editor: No fetched page gives a build year, builder, or restoration date for the Hallowell tower, so the story has no built or staffing section. The firelookout.ca detail page (slug hallowell-fire-lookout, record 13829) returned only the index shell; its record data is loaded by script and was not readable. The brief's county (Sunshine Coast Regional District) is not confirmed by any source read here. Read budget was exceeded: about seven distinct pages were read, including the Rainlander guide, which lists the lookout by name but gives no detail. Two WebSearch calls were used. Fact-check 2026-10-20: the BC Parks page has a 'Visit responsibly' line saying there are no designated hiking and walking trails. That conflicts with its own line that hiking trails lead to Mount Hallowell, and with the Wikipedia description of a well-maintained 1.5 km summit trail. The story keeps the trail claim because two sources state it; an editor may want to confirm the trail with BC Parks.
